sources.name: The AI Daily Brief
sources.description: A daily episode on the most important AI news and what it means, in about half an hour.
sources.overview: A daily solo show about artificial intelligence: the day's headlines first, then one main story argued at length. The beat is AI companies, models, policy, chips and money. The voice is one host thinking aloud, opinionated but careful to say what is reported and what is his own read. Most episodes open with a short statement of the main story, run through shorter headlines, read sponsor messages, and then spend most of the time on the main story with quotes from posts and articles.

robots.finding: Allows everything for every robot except /admin, /api/admin and one sponsor page. Read 2026-11-14.

licence.finding: No licence statement was found: not in agent.json, not in llms.txt, and there is no page at /terms (404).

terms_of_use.finding: The site publishes agent.json and llms.txt as a machine-readable offering for agents, listing a page, a markdown twin, structured JSON and a transcript for each edition. That invites reading; it says nothing about republishing.

terms.summary: The publisher offers its editions to agents in machine-readable form and its robots file allows reading. No licence allows republishing transcripts, so only digests with a link back are published.
uncertain: Whether the publisher is content with short quoted excerpts in a public digest. Reading is clearly invited; republishing is not addressed. Asking the publisher would settle it.

sources.name: Podcasting 2.0
sources.description: The weekly board meeting of the Podcast Index: open podcasting, its standards, apps and money.
sources.overview: A long weekly conversation between the two people who run the Podcast Index. The beat is open podcasting: the podcast namespace and its tags, hosting companies and apps, value for value payments, and what the large platforms are doing. The voice is informal and joking, with strong opinions and a lot of insider shorthand. An episode usually opens with banter, works through the week's news and developer mail, thanks supporters by name, and runs well over an hour.

robots.finding: No robots file on the feed host (404), so nothing is restricted. The transcript host (mp3s.nashownotes.com) has one that disallows nothing and asks for ten seconds between requests.

licence.finding: The feed states no licence and no copyright line. It is marked podcast:locked, which is about moving the feed to another host, not about the content.

terms.summary: The feed and its SubRip transcripts are public and no robots rule restricts them. No licence allows republishing transcripts, so only digests with a link back are published.
uncertain: The show is produced on a value-for-value basis and its makers promote open use of feeds, but no licence says so in writing. If the owner wants full transcripts published, ask the publisher.

sources.name: Build Your SaaS
sources.description: The founders of a small podcast hosting company talk through running it. Episodes are occasional.
sources.overview: An occasional conversation among the people who run Transistor, a small podcast hosting company. The beat is building and running a bootstrapped software business: customers, support, pricing, hiring, and how the founders feel about it. The voice is candid and unhurried, two or three named speakers, often with a guest from the team. An episode is one conversation on one question, around forty minutes, with chapter marks in the notes. Months can pass between episodes.

robots.finding: The transcript host allows everything for robots in general. The feed host answers 400 for robots.txt, which restricts nothing.

licence.finding: The feed carries a copyright line (Transistor, Inc.) and no licence.

terms_of_use.finding: None found for the show itself. The hosting company's general terms were not read.

terms.summary: The feed and its WebVTT transcripts are public and no robots rule restricts them. The content is under the publisher's copyright with no licence to republish, so only digests with a link back are published.
uncertain: The hosting company's terms of service were not read; they govern its customers more than readers of a feed, but the owner may want to check.

sources.name: Buzzcast
sources.description: A weekly, friendly show about making a podcast: tools, habits and news for people who publish one.
sources.overview: A weekly show from the team at a podcast hosting company, for people who make podcasts. The beat is practical: recording and editing tools, growing an audience, what changed in the podcast apps. The voice is light and friendly, three regular hosts who tease each other, with listener mail read out. Episodes vary from a quarter of an hour to an hour: a short personal opening, one or two main topics, then listener messages.

robots.finding: Disallows one unrelated feed only; the show's feed and transcript files are not restricted.

licence.finding: The feed carries a copyright line (Buzzsprout) and no licence. It is marked podcast:locked.

terms_of_use.finding: None found for the show itself. The hosting company's general terms were not read.

terms.summary: The feed and its transcripts are public and no robots rule restricts them. The content is under the publisher's copyright with no licence to republish, so only digests with a link back are published.
uncertain: The transcript marks a speaker only where the speaker changes, so a quote can be credited to the previous speaker. Speaker names in this source's quotes should be treated as likely, not certain.

sources.name: EFF Deeplinks
sources.description: News and commentary on privacy, free speech and technology law. Headline, a short description and a link.
sources.overview: The blog of a civil liberties organisation, written by its lawyers, technologists and activists. The beat is digital rights: privacy and surveillance, free expression, copyright and patents, security, and how new technology such as AI is regulated. The voice is advocacy: it takes a side and says so, and it cites the bills, cases and filings it argues about. Pieces are articles of a few minutes' reading. Only the headline, a short description and the link are carried here.
sources.attribution: Electronic Frontier Foundation, eff.org, CC BY 4.0

robots.finding: Asks robots in general for thirty seconds between requests; the feed address is not disallowed.

licence.finding: Original material on the site may be freely distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence unless noted otherwise; material not original to the publisher may need permission.

terms_of_use.finding: Redistribution with a note of where it came from is appreciated.

terms.summary: Original material is under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. This project still carries only the headline, a short description and the link, with credit, and never the article text.
uncertain: A piece may include material that is not the publisher's own and is not under the same licence. Carrying only the headline, the opening sentences and the link keeps clear of that.
